design.question: [scripted] Do remembered grievances drive cycles of war among the simulated Mediterranean powers?
design.hypothesis: [scripted] Withholding agents' memory of how others treated them reduces the number of wars declared.
design.competing_hypothesis: [scripted] Memory does not change how often the simulated powers go to war.

ir.question: In the Noeterra simulation of mediterranean-264bc, how does withholding every agent's memory of how others have treated it change wars declared over the horizon over 40 seasons, against matched-seed controls?
ir.hypothesis: Withholding every agent's memory of how others have treated it will decrease wars_declared by at least 50 count on average over matched seeds, in the expected direction in at least 4 of 6 seeds.

observables.description: wars declared in breach of a non-aggression pact
soldiers lost or scattered in battle
alliances, pacts and trade agreements concluded
alliances broken by a refused call to arms
Herfindahl index of province shares among surviving civilizations
share of owned provinces held by the largest civilization
fraction of turns that ended with no war in progress
mean stability of surviving civilizations at the end
population of all provinces at the end
provinces held by no civilization at the end
treatment minus control wars_declared, averaged over seeds

independent_variables: withholding every agent's memory of how others have treated it
controls: matched seeds: each seed runs once with and once without the treatment
identical scenario, horizon and rule-based agents in both arms
the engine version is bound into the plan digest
parameter_constraints: closed treatment vocabulary validated by the engine before execution
rule-based agents only, so every run re-simulates exactly
at most 12800 simulated seasons per experiment
3-32 distinct seeds; the effect must appear in at least half of them

statistical_analysis.method: Matched-seed paired difference of the primary metric; per-seed sign counts; frozen rain-criteria/v1
statistical_analysis.uncertainty: Seeds are independent replicates of one illustrative model; descriptive only, no p-value or population inference, and nothing about the historical world.

limitations: Noeterra is an illustrative model: its economy, warfare and diplomacy are invented rules, not estimates of how past societies worked.
Scenario figures are game values; the polities and rulers follow the standard record only as a setting.
A result characterizes the simulator and its agents' policy, not history, and is never empirical evidence.
Agents are the deterministic rule-based policy; model-driven agents are not admitted as experiments.
Native and WebAssembly builds of this engine version reproduce identical state hashes; other versions are refused.

guards.note: An independent re-simulation reproduces every state hash

failure.note: No effect or the opposite direction
